\chapter{One reflexive relation, held as a whole}
\label{ch:sa-bounded-reflexive}
\hlchaptermodality{273}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say one attested sentence in which the object points back to the first-person subject.}

Complete chapter 273 by independently retrieving the bounded reflexive sentence a second time.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{अहमेव} \sk{स्वात्मानं} \sk{न} … (ahameva …)}{अहमेव स्वात्मानं न … (ahameva …)}]{One reflexive relation, held as a whole}

\label{lesson:SA-C273-meet-one-reflexive}



\begin{quote}
Recall the known \sk{आत्मा}, “the self” or “the soul.” Today that known word helps you hear who an object points back to inside one sentence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: one complete attested sentence}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\sk{अहमेव} \sk{स्वात्मानं} \sk{न} \sk{वेद्मि।}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ahameva svātmānaṃ na vedmi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
“I myself do not know my own self.”
\end{quote}

This complete attested sentence appears in Central Sanskrit University's \href{https://www.sanskrit.nic.in/ASSP/Vikramcharitam/6frame7.htm}{\emph{Ādhunika Saṃskṛta Sāhitya Pustakālaya}}. The lesson preserves the source sentence rather than silently composing a new Sanskrit line from the English meaning.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: notice one relation}]
In this one whole line, the speaker is “I.” The form \textbf{\sk{स्वात्मानम्}} is the object and points back to the first-person subject: the speaker does not know the speaker's own self.

Keep the complete sentence together. This lesson does not teach every reflexive form, the middle voice, or a productive method for building new case forms or sandhi combinations.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Read the sentence once slowly. Then say it as one admission: “I myself do not know my own self.”

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say the complete line once more. Keep the object-to-speaker relation inside this attested sentence.
\end{tcolorbox}
